ink.note: There is no ramp. Apparent tone is produced by four ordered dither densities of this one value on paper, never by a lighter colour.

paper.note: Every reading surface, and the ink colour of anything inverted.

display.purpose: 48px Silkscreen. Register counts, the recommended set size, the session score. Always in reserved digit slots.

headline.purpose: 32px Silkscreen from sm up (40px on the landing hero only); 24px on a phone.

body.purpose: 15px Source Sans 3. Explanations, descriptions, list rows.

narrative.overview:
Unit 3 of this syllabus is two-state data representation, so the interface is rendered in two states. There are exactly two colours — ink (#000000) and paper (#ffffff) — and every apparent grey is an ordered dither: real black pixels on white, on a 4x4 tile painted at 4px, 1:1, never scaled. Surfaces are windows: 1px black chrome, a Silkscreen title bar, content on solid white, tiled on a 50% dither desktop. The interface is the curriculum, not a costume.

The build refuses the practice-app dashboard outright: no coloured progress rings, no green ticks, no red crosses. Correctness cannot be a colour here because there is no colour, so every state is carried by pattern and form — marching ants for selection and focus, inversion for the live thing, dither density for confidence and unavailability, dashed chrome for 'quieter' and 'not measured'. What the old system had to promise about not relying on colour is structural here.

Emphasis is inversion, and it is the loudest thing the system owns, so it is rationed to one inverted element per viewport. On the dashboard that is START THIS SET; inside the runner it is the primary control while a question is open, handed to the correct option the moment an answer lands. Title bars, nav tabs, and badges are ink on white and stay that way. Density is high and rhythm is tight (12px inline, 16px block, 12px between windows) because the target device is a mid-range Android on mobile data and the student is a tired fifteen-year-old on a bus.
keyCharacteristics: Two colours only; every tone is a 4x4 ordered dither at 1:1
Zero radius, zero shadow — both Tailwind namespaces reset to initial
Inversion as the only accent, one per viewport
Silkscreen for chrome and numerals, Source Sans 3 for reading
Quantities in reserved digit slots that align down a register
56px touch floor as the default, not the exception
Whole-pixel everything: type sizes, icon grids, dither tiles, steps() motion

rules.name: The Two Values Rule
rules.body: Tailwind's entire --color-* namespace is reset to initial; only ink, paper, transparent, and current are redefined. A third colour is not a policy here, it is unexpressible — there is no utility that can type it.

rules.name: The Never-Scaled Rule
rules.body: A dither is always background-size: 4px 4px on a whole-pixel grid. A dither at any other scale is a moire, not a tone.

rules.name: The Content-Off-The-Dither Rule
rules.body: Long-form reading always happens on solid paper. Where a dither must sit under words — the disabled control — the words get their own paper plate (button:disabled > .btn-label, 6px inline padding). Both rules hold only if the ground is dithered and the words are not; neither 25% nor 12% alone survives a 2px Silkscreen stem.

rules.name: The One Inversion Rule
rules.body: At most one inverted element per viewport, and it marks the live thing: the primary action, the current question, the selected option. Window chrome, navigation, and badges are never inverted — a live title bar was built during this session and deleted before ship.

rules.name: The 16px Floor Rule
rules.body: Silkscreen is never set below 16px. Its ladder in this build is 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 — whole-pixel steps only. At 8px this face has roughly 4px of cap height and is not readable.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is on body. Every digit in the product is the same width, everywhere, always.

rules.name: The Placeholder-Speaks-Chrome Rule
rules.body: A placeholder cannot be grey text here, and grey text was always the weakest way to say it. ::placeholder takes the pixel voice at 14px, uppercase, full-opacity ink; the value speaks in the reading voice. The distinction survives at any contrast setting.

rules.name: The One-Screen Rule
rules.body: A session owns the whole viewport. Persistent chrome and the bottom nav both return null under /session/; a student answering a question has exactly one thing in front of them.

rules.name: The Wrap-Above-Scroll-Below Rule
rules.body: The question palette wraps at sm:flex-wrap and scrolls horizontally below it, with the current cell scrolled to centre on change. Full 56px targets and a whole-paper overview only conflict inside a single row.

rules.name: The Flat Raster Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts. If a surface needs to separate from what is behind it, give it chrome or change its ground's density — never a shadow, never a blur, never opacity.

dos: Do build every surface as a Window: 1px ink chrome, Silkscreen title bar, content on solid paper.
Do spend the viewport's one inversion on the live thing — the primary action, the current question, the selected option — and hand it over when the live thing changes.
Do keep Silkscreen at 16 / 24 / 32 / 48px and Source Sans 3 for anything longer than a label.
Do carry state with pattern and form: ants for selection and focus, dither density for confidence and unavailability, dashed chrome for quieter, the word alongside every verdict mark.
Do give a disabled control a 25% dither ground, dashed chrome, and a paper plate under its label.
Do distinguish unmeasured (12% dither, dashed) from measured-at-zero (25% empty cells). This is the product's honesty rule rendered, and it must survive every future change.
Do put quantities in reserved digit slots so they align down the column, and draw zeroes as zeroes.
Do hold a 56px minimum on anything a student taps; 44px exists only for mouse-driven admin chrome.
Do let windows go full-bleed below sm (border-y / sm:border-x, containers px-0 sm:px-4).
Do invert secondary controls and nav links on hover.
Do time every animation in steps() and stop all of it under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't introduce a third value, a gradient, or an opacity that manufactures a grey. Two colours and four dither densities is the whole material set.
Don't round a corner or cast a shadow — the namespaces are reset; there is nothing to reach for.
Don't invert a title bar, a nav item, or a badge. Chrome is not the live thing.
Don't scale a dither. background-size is 4px 4px, always.
Don't set body text on a dither, and don't set a Silkscreen label on one without a paper plate.
Don't synthesise bold or italic on the pixel voice.
Don't draw a bar at zero for something that has not been measured.
Don't carry a verdict on a mark alone; the word ships beside every check and cross.
Don't import a stroked or rounded icon set. Icons are filled cells on a 12x12 grid at whole multiples.
Don't add decorative pixel art, a fake menu bar, or a trash can. If a pixel is not carrying information, it is not in the design.
